question: SQ-LIP-000008
text: Is lipedema associated with fibromyalgia and other chronic-pain conditions?
minor_problems: [minor] set: E5 (34% fibromyalgia, 354-woman survey wording identical to E4) likely re-reports the same cohort as E4 but has no secondary_of, so prevalence may be counted twice.
[minor] set: P2 contains context items (E3, E27) that are unrelated to its statement; P5 mixes symptoms with comorbidities.

[minor] P2: not fully supported; overgeneralized; two ideas; misplaced ['E3', 'E27'] — suggested: Pain is reported by most people with lipedema and appears more frequent and more disabling than in matched comparison groups. (High prevalence of pain is supported (E6, E12, E26), but the comparative claim rests on E6 only among the listed items. E2 (90.3% vs 42.7% leg pain) would support the comparison and is placed under P5. E3 (fibromyalgia scores unchanged after a diet) and E27 (comorbidity list) do not bear on pain prevalence or disability.)

[minor] P5: not fully supported; overgeneralized; two ideas; misplaced ['E8', 'E2'] — suggested: Joint pain, arthritis and migraine are reported as comorbidities in a substantial share of people with lipedema, with prevalences varying across samples. (Bundles joint pain, arthritis and migraine whose prevalence differs a lot (migraine 8.4% to 35%); 'frequently' is too strong for the low end. E8 (hypermobility, fatigue) and E2 (knee/leg pain symptom) are symptoms, not comorbid conditions. The post-surgical migraine improvement in E14 is not a comorbidity finding.)

[minor] P6: not fully supported; overgeneralized — suggested: In obese women with lipedema on a low-carbohydrate or low-fat diet, pain reduction may not be mediated by changes in systemic inflammatory or fibrotic markers. (Single RCT secondary analysis restricted to dietary intervention; the statement generalises to any pain reduction. Also peripheral to the fibromyalgia/chronic-pain association question.)

propositions.statement: Fibromyalgia is frequently reported to co-occur with lipedema in cross-sectional studies, although reported frequencies vary widely between samples.
propositions.rationale: Several cross-sectional samples using fibromyalgia criteria find substantial co-occurrence in both directions, with one comparison reporting a lower frequency.

evidence.finding: Among 100 women meeting fibromyalgia criteria, lipedema was found in 50% (58% stage 1); longer fibromyalgia diagnostic delay associated with lipedema.
In an online survey of 354 women with lipedema, 35% (124/354) met ACR 2016 fibromyalgia criteria; those with fibromyalgia had higher anxiety, depression and worse quality of life.
34% of women with lipedema met ACR 2016 criteria for comorbid fibromyalgia; comparison of fibromyalgia and lipedema cohorts showed phenotypic overlap.
39.6% (21/53) of lipedema patients met ACR 2016 fibromyalgia criteria; the comorbid subgroup had higher pain (median VAS 60 vs 27, p<0.001) and worse SF-36 scores in all domains.
Fibromyalgia was reported in 10% of lipedema patients versus 28% in Dercum's disease (P=0.0003); crude, unadjusted prevalences.
In a survey of lipedema patients, fibromyalgia was among the most frequently reported comorbidities (n=14); comorbidities were associated with reduced quality of life.
A proposed mechanistic framework cites a 35-40% comorbidity of lipedema with fibromyalgia.

propositions.statement: Pain is reported by most people with lipedema and is more frequent and more disabling than in matched comparison groups.
propositions.rationale: Controlled and uncontrolled cross-sectional data and reviews consistently describe pain as a near-universal, disabling feature of lipedema.

evidence.finding: Versus sex-, age- and BMI-matched population controls, no lipedema patient was pain-free (vs 29.2% of controls); pain-related disability in daily activities much higher (p<0.001); pain correlated with depressive symptoms (rho=0.612).
In 381 lipedema patients, pain was reported by 87.9% (BPI>=7 in 14.2%) and high fatigue by 56.1%; fibromyalgia not separately quantified.
Pain was present in most women with lipedema regardless of BMI, stage or morphological type, and correlated most strongly with touch hypersensitivity and leg heaviness.
Fibromyalgia (FAS) and VAS pain scores did not change significantly after four weeks of a modified Mediterranean diet in lipoedema (FAS p=0.75; VAS p=0.47).
Narrative review states lipedema leads to chronic pain, swelling and other discomforts; no fibromyalgia data.
Narrative review states delayed diagnosis of lipedema often results in fibrosis, lymphatic dysfunction, chronic pain and functional impairment.
Narrative review lists hypertension, anemia, anxiety and depression as common comorbidities and describes a multifactorial pain mechanism; no fibromyalgia association reported.

propositions.statement: Lipedema is associated with lower pressure pain thresholds than in healthy or obese comparison groups.
propositions.rationale: Case-control and cross-sectional studies with quantitative sensory testing find pressure hyperalgesia in lipedema, with disagreement on whether it is localized or widespread.

evidence.finding: In 24 women with lipedema vs 20 BMI-matched healthy controls, pressure pain thresholds were significantly lower at all assessed regions (p<0.001).
Obese women with lipedema (n=30) vs obesity alone (n=29) had higher pain intensity, lower pressure pain thresholds in arms and legs, greater pain interference and catastrophizing (p<0.05).

Cited quantitative sensory testing in non-obese women: pressure pain threshold reduced 2-fold and vibration detection threshold raised 2.5-fold selectively in the affected thigh, not the hand, suggesting a peripheral mechanism.

propositions.statement: Neuropathic pain features are frequently reported in lipedema and may be more common in advanced stages.
propositions.rationale: Several studies using neuropathic pain screening tools find such features in lipedema, more than in lymphedema, with stage-dependent findings.

evidence.finding: In 118 women, lipedema patients had higher pain severity (VAS 6.2 vs 5.5, p=0.02) and neuropathic pain prevalence (42% vs 21%, p<0.01) than lymphedema patients.
In 20 women with lipedema vs 20 healthy controls, lipedema patients showed clinically relevant pain and neuropathic pain features (VAS, LANSS, DN4); LANSS correlated with VAS (rho=0.529).
Among women with lower extremity pain, probable lipedema was more frequent than in controls (36.8% vs 12.3%, p=0.001); PainDETECT independently associated with LSQ score (beta=0.382, p=0.004).
painDETECT scores were higher in stage 3 (17.6) than stages 1-2 (11.0, 10.5; p=0.0271), with neuropathic responders only in stage 3; cutaneous hypersensitivity and CGRP/NGF increased with stage.

propositions.statement: Other chronic pain conditions, such as joint pain, arthritis and migraine, are frequently reported as comorbidities of lipedema.
propositions.rationale: Descriptive cohorts and surveys report high crude frequencies of joint pain, arthritis, migraine and hypermobility in lipedema.

evidence.finding: In 860 lipedema patients, 99% had at least one comorbidity: joint pain 58%, insomnia 36%, migraine 35%, depression 31%; fibromyalgia not listed.
Online survey: lipedema patients reported chronic joint pain (ankles 70%, cervical spine 66%, knees 56%) more often than lymphedema patients; differences not statistically tested.
In 189 women undergoing reduction surgery: joint hypermobility 50.5%, arthritis 29.1% (knee 15.8%), depression 22.8%, migraine 8.4%; crude prevalences.
22.6% of lipedema patients undergoing liposuction had a prior migraine diagnosis; 66.7% of them reported reduced intensity or frequency after surgery (p<0.0001).
Chart review and literature describe severe pain, fatigue (~75%), gait abnormalities and hypermobility in >50% of lipedema patients.
In a population screening, knee pain was reported by 58.1% of screen-positive women; leg pain 90.3% vs 42.7% in screen-negative women.

propositions.statement: Pain reduction in lipedema may not be mediated by changes in systemic inflammatory or fibrotic markers.
propositions.rationale: A randomised diet trial found pain changes unrelated to systemic cytokine or fibrosis marker changes, qualifying inflammatory explanations of lipedema pain.

evidence.finding: In a randomised low-carbohydrate vs low-fat diet trial, pain changes at week 9 were not associated with changes in hsCRP, cytokines, fibrotic markers or ketosis, in ITT or PP analyses.

Off-topic: review about diagnostic and management challenges, no finding on fibromyalgia or chronic-pain comorbidity.

verdicts.note: Supported by several ACR 2016 prevalence figures (35-40%), with E11 (10%) correctly as refines. E1 is the reverse direction (lipedema among fibromyalgia patients). E5 reports 34% and appears to re-report the same 354-woman cohort as E4 (identical old_statement) without secondary_of; E20 is a secondary citation.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Pain is reported by most people with lipedema and appears more frequent and more disabling than in matched comparison groups.
verdicts.note: High prevalence of pain is supported (E6, E12, E26), but the comparative claim rests on E6 only among the listed items. E2 (90.3% vs 42.7% leg pain) would support the comparison and is placed under P5. E3 (fibromyalgia scores unchanged after a diet) and E27 (comorbidity list) do not bear on pain prevalence or disability.
E24 and E21 are primary controlled comparisons; E19 is a review citing QST data consistent with the statement.
Stage-dependence rests on a single study (E9) but is hedged with 'may'. E25 is a screening association (reverse direction) but adds a PainDETECT link.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Joint pain, arthritis and migraine are reported as comorbidities in a substantial share of people with lipedema, with prevalences varying across samples.
verdicts.note: Bundles joint pain, arthritis and migraine whose prevalence differs a lot (migraine 8.4% to 35%); 'frequently' is too strong for the low end. E8 (hypermobility, fatigue) and E2 (knee/leg pain symptom) are symptoms, not comorbid conditions. The post-surgical migraine improvement in E14 is not a comorbidity finding.

verdicts.suggested_statement: In obese women with lipedema on a low-carbohydrate or low-fat diet, pain reduction may not be mediated by changes in systemic inflammatory or fibrotic markers.
verdicts.note: Single RCT secondary analysis restricted to dietary intervention; the statement generalises to any pain reduction. Also peripheral to the fibromyalgia/chronic-pain association question.

set_issues.issue: E5 (34% fibromyalgia, 354-woman survey wording identical to E4) likely re-reports the same cohort as E4 but has no secondary_of, so prevalence may be counted twice.
P2 contains context items (E3, E27) that are unrelated to its statement; P5 mixes symptoms with comorbidities.
